aliases.name: UAC-0165
aliases.vendor: SSSCIP (Ukraine), described as a Sandworm subgroup tied to the ISP attacks

identification.summary: Solntsepek (also spelled Solntsepyok) is a Telegram-based hacktivist-style persona that claims disruptive and hack-and-leak attacks against Ukrainian targets [S1][S3]. Ukraine's SSSCIP tracks the actor behind the March 2024 ISP attacks as UAC-0165, which it describes as a Sandworm subgroup [S4]. Mandiant lists Solntsepek, XakNet Team and CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn (CARR) as three Telegram personas used by Sandworm (APT44), operating in parallel and independently of one another [S5][S6]. Mandiant's John Hultquist said the persona was probably fabricated by the GRU to launder its operations publicly [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Earliest dated claim in the gathered sources: June 2023 (Suspilne websites) [S7]. Mandiant reports the channel leaked personal data of Ukrainian military and security personnel before a 2023 rebrand to a 'hacker group' [S3].
identification.notes: Persona, not a separate organization, per Ukrainian and Mandiant assessments [S2][S5]. Do not merge Solntsepek facts with Sandworm/APT44 intrusion facts (e.g., the Kyivstar intrusion dating to at least May 2023 is SBU's finding about Sandworm, not a Solntsepek claim) [S2]. MITRE group id and Microsoft name are blank in this record; Microsoft tracks Sandworm as Seashell Blizzard but that mapping was not verified in these sources.

attribution.sponsor: Russian military intelligence (GRU), via the Sandworm cluster, according to Ukrainian authorities and Mandiant [S2][S4][S5].
attribution.confidence: Ukraine's SBU said it is a GRU subdivision-linked front and that many indicators suggest Solntsepek was behind the March 2024 ISP attacks; SBU's investigation was ongoing [S4]. SBU cyber chief Illia Vitiuk said Sandworm was likely responsible for Kyivstar and later that he was 'pretty sure' [S2]. Mandiant assesses the persona is probably GRU-fabricated and says it is unclear how much control Sandworm exerts over its personas [S2][S5]. Russia denied involvement [S1][S2].
attribution.basis: SSSCIP tracking designation UAC-0165 [S4]; SBU investigation of Kyivstar [S2]; Mandiant APT44 reporting on hacktivist personas, as relayed by press [S5][S6]. Primary SBU, SSSCIP and Mandiant documents were not opened; this relies on press coverage.

objectives: Public claiming of disruption and data theft against Ukrainian government, telecom and media targets, aimed at undermining Ukrainian communications supporting the armed forces and at information effects; the group stated its Kyivstar rationale as the company serving the Armed Forces, government and law enforcement [S3]. Mandiant assesses the personas exaggerate impact to serve information goals, including perceptions of popular support for the war [S5].

sectors: Government (Ministry of Communities and Territories Development local network)
Military and security personnel (personal data leaks)
targeting.notes: Claimed victims include Kyivstar (Dec 2023), Triacom, Misto TV, Linktelecom and KIM (claimed 13 Mar 2024), Gigabit-net, Znet, and the sites of Suspilne, Gordon and Channel 24 [S3][S4][S7][S8]. Claims are the persona's own; small ISPs were hard to verify [S4].

capabilities.summary: The persona publishes claims and leaked data on Telegram; reported impact figures (10,000 computers, 4,000 servers at Kyivstar) were disputed by Kyivstar [S2][S3]. Destructive capability is attributed to the underlying Sandworm access: SBU found Sandworm in Kyivstar systems from at least May 2023 with full access probably from about November [S2]. Earlier Solntsepek attacks reportedly caused limited damage [S8].

campaigns.name: Leaks of Ukrainian military and security personnel data
campaigns.summary: Per Mandiant, the Solntsepek channel leaked personally identifiable information of Ukrainian military and security personnel before rebranding as a hacker group [S3].

campaigns.name: Suspilne website attack
campaigns.summary: Suspilne websites went down and Solntsepyok claimed responsibility; CERT-UA investigated [S7].

campaigns.name: Kyivstar attack claim
campaigns.summary: Solntsepek claimed the attack on Kyivstar, alleging 10,000 computers and 4,000 servers destroyed; Kyivstar refuted the figures. SBU linked the persona to Sandworm and found the intrusion dated to at least May 2023.

campaigns.name: Attacks on four Ukrainian ISPs
campaigns.summary: Solntsepek claimed on 13 March the disruption of Triacom, Misto TV, Linktelecom and KIM, which it said served government bodies and parts of the armed forces. Outages reportedly lasted over a week. SSSCIP tied the activity to UAC-0165 (Sandworm subgroup) [S4].

campaigns.name: Mandiant APT44 reporting on personas
campaigns.summary: Mandiant named Solntsepek, XakNet Team and CARR as three Telegram personas used by Sandworm, operating in parallel and independently [S5][S6]. Date approximate (report publication month).

diamond.adversary: GRU-linked Sandworm (APT44) operators presenting as a hacktivist persona; UAC-0165 per SSSCIP [S2][S4][S5].
diamond.capability: Telegram claim-and-leak operations; wiper-style destruction attributed to Sandworm access [S2][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram channel for claims and leaks [S3]. Technical infrastructure not public in the sources gathered.
diamond.victim: Ukrainian telecoms and ISPs, government networks, media outlets, military personnel [S3][S4][S7][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Information operation amplifying disruption of Ukrainian military-supporting infrastructure and projecting domestic support for the war [S3][S5].
diamond.technology: Telecom core and ISP networks and their management systems; web properties of media outlets [S2][S4][S7].

gaps: Primary documents not opened: Mandiant APT44 report, SSSCIP/CERT-UA UAC-0165 advisories, SBU statements; webpages (Kyiv Independent, The Record, The Hacker News, dev.ua) could not be fetched, so claims rely on search-result summaries.
Exact dates of several press items are approximate (month level).
The dev.ua article cited in the existing record (Ministry of Communities, Suspilne, ISPs) was not retrieved.
Technical TTPs, malware and indicators specific to the Solntsepek persona are not established; wiper use in the ISP attacks was not established in the cited sources.
How much operational control Sandworm exerts over Solntsepek is unclear per Mandiant.
Whether the earlier personal-data leaks involved intrusions or recycled data is unknown.
Microsoft name and MITRE group mapping not verified.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Telecom and ISP networks serving military and government users are key terrain in Ukraine and, by analogy, for any theater relying on commercial carriers. STEP 2: A GRU-linked actor uses a hacktivist persona to deniably claim destructive effects and to amplify them [S2][S5]. STEP 3: Long dwell time (months inside Kyivstar before disruption) then destruction, then public claim with inflated figures [S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued claimed attacks on small and mid-size Ukrainian telecoms, media and government networks, timed with information goals. MDCOA is the same persona claiming disruption of commercial carriers or ISPs serving partner or US-supporting forces outside Ukraine, with pre-positioned access activated for effect. Candidate indicators: Telegram claims naming providers that serve military customers, unexplained outages at small ISPs, and unusual administrative access to carrier management systems [S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: monitor persona Telegram channels as early warning, but verify claims before reporting impact since figures were exaggerated [S2][S3]. (2) Authorities: attribution to GRU rests on Ukrainian and vendor assessments; do not elevate it to government attribution without official confirmation. (3) Mission assurance: identify commercial telecom and ISP dependencies for mission-critical connectivity and plan alternate paths, given outages lasting over a week at small ISPs [S4]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with Ukrainian counterparts (SSSCIP, CERT-UA, SBU) and Sandworm/APT44 tracking through established channels.

provenance.importedSummary: Solntsepek is a threat actor group with ties to the Russian military unit GRU. They have claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on Kyivstar, a Ukrainian mobile operator, and have been linked to previous attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. Solntsepek has been associated with the Sandworm hacking group, known for their destructive cyberattacks, including the NotPetya worm. They have also engaged in hostile activities, such as revealing personal details of Ukrainian soldiers.
